title: Iff-split of irreducibility ↔ absolute irreducibility (FLT odd representation)
intent: Split the main result 'ρ is irreducible iff it is absolutely irreducible' into its two directions and close each by one named lemma: the hard direction base-changes irreducibility to the algebraic closure, and the easy direction descends irreducibility from the base change. The glue is a nine-line `constructor` proof that instantiates both lemmas at `AlgebraicClosure k`.

parent.name: isIrreducible_iff_isAbsolutelyIrreducible_slop
parent.statement:
theorem isIrreducible_iff_isAbsolutelyIrreducible_slop
    [FiniteDimensional k V]
    {g : G} (hg : finrank k (Module.End.eigenspace (ρ g) 1) = 1) :
    ρ.IsIrreducible ↔ IsAbsolutelyIrreducible ρ

children.name: isIrreducible_baseChange_of_finrank_eigenspace_eq_one
children.statement:
theorem isIrreducible_baseChange_of_finrank_eigenspace_eq_one
    [FiniteDimensional k V]
    (l : Type*) [Field l] [Algebra k l]
    (hirr : ρ.IsIrreducible)
    {g : G} (hg : finrank k (Module.End.eigenspace (ρ g) 1) = 1) :
    (baseChange l ρ).IsIrreducible
children.closed_by: chains five project lemmas: exists_smul_eq_of_commute (Lemma 1.4), adjoinRange_eq_top (Lemma 1.5), adjoinRange_baseChange_eq_top (Lemma 1.6), isIrreducible_iff_forall (unpacks irreducibility), then isIrreducible_of_adjoinRange_eq_top (step (iv)); lines 453-474

children.name: isIrreducible_of_baseChange
children.statement:
lemma isIrreducible_of_baseChange (l : Type*) [Field l] [Algebra k l]
    (h : (baseChange l ρ).IsIrreducible) :
    ρ.IsIrreducible
children.closed_by: unpacks irreducibility with isIrreducible_iff_forall and descends the invariant subspace via Submodule.baseChange_injective; lines 408-440

applicability.goal_shape: A biconditional P ↔ Q where one side is defined as the other after base change to an algebraic closure (IsAbsolutelyIrreducible ρ := (baseChange (AlgebraicClosure k) ρ).IsIrreducible); each direction is stated as a named lemma over an arbitrary field extension l/k.
applicability.use_when: both directions are genuinely independent named lemmas: the forward direction needs a chain of auxiliary results while the reverse is a short descent, so a `constructor` plus one `exact` per direction is all the glue needed.
applicability.avoid_when: the reverse direction reuses intermediate facts of the forward direction (then it is not a leaf); the two directions are not stated at the same generality (here the hard direction is over any l/k, the easy direction only needs l = AlgebraicClosure k); the definitional side of the iff is not a simple `unfold` away.

consequences: The `constructor` on an ↔ creates exactly two goals (one per direction) and no exhaustiveness obligation. The hard direction is stated over an arbitrary field extension l/k rather than just AlgebraicClosure k, which is what lets the glue instantiate it at AlgebraicClosure k while keeping the lemma reusable elsewhere. The easy direction is a genuine leaf only because its invariant-subspace descent (via Submodule.baseChange_injective) closes on its own; it does not reuse the hard direction's intermediate lemmas, so the two halves can be proved in either order.
